A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SageAttention work. Their complete main text and Appendices A–B, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original attention-kernel benchmarks, model evaluations and ablations in Sections 4–5, with additional quantitative and visual results in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v6 retains original kernel-speed measurements, model-quality evaluations, ablations and appendix comparisons, including Tables 13–19 and generated image/video examples.

M1.justification: K smoothing, quantization choices, FP16 accumulation, adaptive kernel selection and fusion procedures are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the four implementations in Table 6 retain the same content.

E1.justification: The language, image/video generation, classification and visual-question-answering coverage remains unchanged. Section 5.1 and Appendices A.3 and B.2 retain the same datasets and scenarios, including the Open-Sora visual example.

E2.justification: Figures 6–9 retain Torch, xformers and FlashAttention2; Tables 1 and 18 retain quantized FlashAttention3. Tables 13–15 retain the AWQ, Q-diffusion and ViDiT-Q comparisons, respectively.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the RTX4090/3090 benchmarks, head dimensions 64/128, causal/noncausal settings and evaluation metrics. Appendix A also retains the same kernel parameters and selection of 256 COCO validation pairs.

E4.justification: The smoothing, quantization-granularity, data-type, accumulator and adaptive-quantization analyses remain unchanged. Appendix precision comparisons and qualitative image/video examples are also retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same average and worst-layer summaries. Neither reports experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 7 retains the CogvideoX speedup of 2.01x, and Table 8 retains SageAttention's Llama2 WikiText perplexity of 5.824.

T1.justification: The attention and quantization definitions, online-softmax equations, and shift-invariance argument supporting K smoothing are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: plug-and-play attention acceleration, approximately 2.1x/2.7x speedups over FlashAttention2/xformers, and negligible end-to-end metric loss.

C2.justification: The outlier explanation, hardware-performance rationale, interpretation of results and broader-applicability discussion retain the same meaning. Appendix A.6 changes citations without adding mechanisms, limitations or applicability claims.

D1.justification: Code and example-access disclosures are unchanged. Appendix A.1–A.3 retains the same hardware, software versions, kernel hyperparameters, model identification and data-selection instructions.

R1.justification: The additional SageAttention2 and SpargeAttn bibliography entries are alternate-title/year versions of works already cited in v5. Matching these works leaves the research coverage and positioning unchanged; Section 2 is identical.

P1.justification: v6 merges the Performance Analysis paragraph into the preceding paragraph in Section 4.6, adds alternate bibliography entries, adjusts citation labels and punctuation, and updates the arXiv stamp. Section order and scientific prose otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: Local spacing and page-flow adjustments shift existing displays vertically and move the concluding Section 5.3 sentences from page 10 to page 9. Figure/table content, captions and structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 retains v5's complete methods, main and appendix evidence, and reproducibility information. The alternate reference entries, paragraph-boundary edits and small layout adjustments have no meaningful net effect on scientific support or overall readability.
